nameStory: The "two-flower" part of this plant's name comes from its tendency to produce exactly two bright yellow blooms per flower stalk, like nature's perfect pair of sunny eyes. The "dwarf-dandelion" part reflects both its modest height compared to regular dandelions and its similar cheerful yellow flowers, though it's actually not closely related to true dandelions at all.
description: Two-flower Dwarf-dandelion is a perennial wildflower that stands 18-31 inches tall with bright yellow-orange daisy-like flowers. Each plant produces multiple flower stalks, typically bearing two blooms per stalk, creating clusters of sunny flowers that brighten meadows and streambanks. The flowers are quite showy for such a modestly-named plant, measuring about 1-1.5 inches across with numerous narrow ray petals radiating from the center. This spreading plant can form colonies over time, making impressive displays when in full bloom.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Bright yellow to orange-yellow daisy-like flowers, 1-1.5 inches across, with 25-60 narrow ray petals and no central disc flowers - just pure rays of sunshine

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Characteristically produces two flowers per stalk (though sometimes just one), with multiple stalks per plant creating clusters of paired blooms

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Erect perennial reaching 18-31 inches tall, often spreading aggressively to form colonies

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: One plant can produce 20 or more flower heads, creating impressive displays when multiple stalks bloom simultaneously

habitat: Look for Two-flower Dwarf-dandelion in moist, open areas like streambanks, wet meadows, and prairie edges. It thrives in various soil types but prefers consistently moist conditions, making it most common near water sources or in low-lying areas that stay damp through the growing season.

seasonality.spring: Plants emerge and begin developing flower stalks in late spring, with the earliest blooms appearing as temperatures warm.
seasonality.summer: Peak blooming period extends through summer with multiple flushes of bright yellow flowers creating showy displays.
seasonality.fall: Blooming can continue into early fall in favorable conditions, with plants beginning to set seed and die back.
seasonality.winter: Plants die back completely, surviving underground as perennial roots that will re-emerge the following spring.

funFact: Despite being called a "dwarf" dandelion, this plant can actually grow taller than common dandelions and puts on a much more impressive flower show - one plant can produce over 20 flower heads compared to dandelion's typical single bloom per stalk!
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with common dandelions, but Two-flower Dwarf-dandelion is much taller, produces multiple flowers per stalk (usually two), and has more ray petals per flower head. Remember: dandelions are low rosettes with single flowers, while this species stands tall with paired blooms.
contextualKnowledge: This plant is quite rare in New England, especially Connecticut where it's listed as a species of special concern - so consider yourself lucky if you spot one! The genus name honors David Krieg, a German physician who first collected specimens in colonial Maryland.
compareHints: Two-flower Dwarf-dandelion differs from its relative Virginia Dwarf-dandelion by being much taller (18-31 inches vs. just a few inches), having more flowers per plant, and typically producing two flowers per stalk rather than single blooms. Virginia Dwarf-dandelion stays close to the ground in a rosette form, while Two-flower stands proudly upright.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Virginia dwarfdandelion differs from its relative two-flower dwarf-dandelion by typically having just one flower per stem (rather than two or more) and smaller overall size.
